claims.claim: Compare-mode pick-winner runs still produce null telemetry selection basis: `ResolveCompare` sets the winner but never sets `selection_basis` or `spine_tiebreak`, while manifest telemetry only projects those two fields into `telemetry.judge.selection_basis`.

A valid single-provider build whose baseline gate fails before providers launch will be reported invalid by `runs verify`: the build path emits `baseline_failed` or `baseline_expectation_failed` while preserving `run_mode: single_provider`, but verify accepts only `single_provider_result` and `single_provider_failed` for every single-provider run.

`runs verify` does not enforce the successful single-provider build handoff contract: if a `single_provider_result` build decision loses `selected_patch_provider`, the dynamic required patch artifact check returns no selected-patch requirements and the single-provider semantic check only requires a non-empty `single_provider`.

The new truncation alarm suppression can hide real stderr loss: successful provider stderr is classified as `diagnostic` even when it contains a trailing `ERROR`, and `output_truncation_count` now ignores truncated diagnostic stderr for successful providers.

Run-id collision safety regressed for incomplete research directories: any existing run directory with only the allowlisted scaffold files is removed without checking that its archived `work-order.json` matches the work order being launched, so reusing a run id can silently overwrite a different incomplete run.

Experiment manifest fallback is still fragile for partial metadata: a non-empty `meta.experiment` prevents falling back to `work-order.json`, so stale or partial meta can drop otherwise validated experiment fields such as `repetition_index`, `slot_id`, or `slot_attempt` from the manifest.
